newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican airport closes, fire engulfs solvent depot.
newsitem.headline: Mexican airport closes, fire engulfs solvent depot.

text.p: A huge fire engulfed a solvent depot at the Toluca International Airport near Mexico City on Monday, forcing authorities to halt flights, officials said.
Flames leapt 100 feet (33 metres) into the air at the mostly-freight terminal 25 miles (40 km) west of the capital. No casualties were immediately reported.
Authorities did not give the cause of the blaze, which broke out at dawn, belching smoke over a wide area. The Televisa television netowrk said the fire was just 20 yards (metres) from the runway.
Dozens of firemen fought the blaze for an hour before getting it under control.
"It is now totally contained," said Alfredo Valdez, police chief of Mexico state, of which Toluca is the capital.
Valdez said there was no danger to life or to air traffic, and normal scheduled and charter flights would resume soon.
Toluca airport backs up Mexico City's Benito Juarez International Airport, taking considerable freight traffic.
